title: Periodic boundaries and image interactions for hierarchical solvers
numerical_oracle: Direct CPU strict reference with minimum-image displacement

scope.domain: box wrap, minimum-image fold, and periodic cell acceptance for Octree-based short-range interactions

periodic_domain.box_origin: Vector3 finite origin; period starts at origin and repeats with stride size
periodic_domain.box_size: Vector3 positive, finite Lx, Ly, Lz; the same value is used for the wrap and the fold
periodic_domain.wrap: coordinates are folded into [origin, origin + size) along every axis
periodic_domain.minimum_image: a displacement is folded per axis into (-size/2, size/2]; only the nearest image of a distinct source can fall within the interaction window
periodic_domain.interaction_window: Rc is bounded by min(Lx, Ly, Lz) / 2, which guarantees at most one image of each source lies inside Rc; every pair contributes its minimum-image displacement and the window does not truncate the force, so the windowed 27-region enumeration is exactly equivalent to the minimum-image reference inside Rc
periodic_domain.disabled: when periodic boundaries are disabled the wrap, fold, and containment reduce exactly to the open-boundary identity; the non-periodic CPU path is bit-identical to the baseline

image_regions.enumeration: 3 x 3 x 3 lattice of periodic copies of the box
image_regions.central: the primary copy that holds the physical sources (region index 0)
image_regions.neighbors: the 26 surrounding regions: 6 face regions with a single axis shift, 12 edge regions with two axis shifts, and 8 corner regions with three axis shifts
image_regions.candidate_rule: a source contributes exactly one image inside Rc; that image is the minimum-image displacement, so the 26 neighboring regions plus the central copy are the complete set of candidates inside Rc
image_regions.ordering: image regions are enumerated deterministically: z, then y, then x, each in order 0, +1, -1 shift with the central region first

hierarchy.no_duplication: periodic interactions reuse the single Octree built over the wrapped box; no per-image tree copy is created
hierarchy.folded_geometry: leaf sources, multipole displacements, far-cell equivalent points, and cell containment all use minimum-image geometry against the wrapped box
hierarchy.no_double_count: each physical source is visited at most once per target and contributes its single nearest image
hierarchy.refit_parity: a refit pass and a full rebuild produce the same periodic forces for the same wrapped state

scope.input_convention: source and target coordinates are wrapped into the box before planning and evaluation; the periodic domain exposes the wrap for the caller and the solvers consume already-wrapped state

planned_cases.name: periodic-domain-semantics
planned_cases.contract: wrap folds coordinates into the box; minimum image folds per axis into (-size/2, size/2]; the 26 neighboring regions are enumerated deterministically with the central copy first; disabled boundaries act as the identity; invalid boxes are rejected

planned_cases.name: reference-window-equivalence
planned_cases.contract: the Direct periodic reference equals the summed interaction of the central copy plus the 26 surrounding regions after window reduction: each pair contributes exactly its nearest image inside Rc and no other region is within Rc

planned_cases.name: bh-periodic-parity
planned_cases.contract: Barnes-Hut with periodic boundaries matches the Direct periodic reference within the declared relative tolerance, and bit-exactly as the opening angle vanishes

planned_cases.name: fmm-periodic-parity
planned_cases.contract: FMM with periodic boundaries matches the Direct periodic reference within the declared relative tolerance

planned_cases.name: kifmm-periodic-parity
planned_cases.contract: KIFMM with periodic boundaries matches the Direct periodic reference within the declared relative tolerance

planned_cases.name: seam-no-double-count
planned_cases.contract: a pair straddling the wrap seam receives exactly one interaction: isolated-pair forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and equal to the minimum-image single-pair force rather than to a multiple-image sum

planned_cases.name: open-boundary-unchanged
planned_cases.contract: with periodic boundaries disabled every solver produces bit-identical forces to the existing non-periodic CPU baseline

planned_cases.name: refit-and-rebuild-parity
planned_cases.contract: periodic forces are identical whether the Octree is built fresh or built then refit for the same wrapped state

planned_cases.name: mpi-race-lane
planned_cases.contract: PBC interaction with domain-decomposition halos, migration, restart, and changed-rank-count runs is coordinated with the P7/P8 MPI lanes and the P5 grid mesh; it is capability-gated on the local single-rank qualification path

acceptance.implementation_registration: convert planned cases into TST-P3 identifiers and CTest entries; PBC-AC-009 registers as a capability-gated lane
acceptance.qualification: CPU strict reference is mandatory; MPI halo, migration, restart, and rank-change PBC qualification is capability-gated

tolerances.reference_parity: relative L2 force error below 0.05 at the default hierarchical opening angle, matching the established P3 tree-solver acceptance
tolerances.exact_gate: bit-exact equality against the Direct periodic reference at opening angle zero for the tree solvers
tolerances.open_boundary: bit parity with the existing non-periodic CPU lane

non_goals.no_tree_duplication: no per-image copy of the Octree hierarchy is introduced
non_goals.no_ewald_long_range: lattice-sum regularization of the replicated gravitational system (Ewald, P3M mesh, TreePM long range) is not implemented by P3-PBC-001; coordination is deferred to the grid and multipole mesh lanes
non_goals.no_grid_periodicity: the P5 Grid resource and PM/TreePM mesh remain non-periodic under this contract
non_goals.no_ode_periodicity: no periodic correction is applied to position integration; only the force interaction geometry is periodic

coordination.grid_boundary: grid-mesh periodic deposition and halo exchange coordinate with issue 695
coordination.ewald_mesh: long-range lattice-sum regularization coordinates with the multipole-mesh dependency
coordination.mpi_pbc: PBC across domain boundaries coordinates with the P7/P8 MPI lanes and remains capability-gated until a multi-rank lane exists
coordination.short_range_window: the Rc bound subsumes the local-neighborhood window of plan/neighborhood.json so a distinct source has at most one contributing image inside Rc

migration.open_boundary_is_default: absence of a periodic domain retains the exact non-periodic behavior, so no legacy configuration is reinterpreted
migration.input_wrapping: the caller wraps state before evaluation; the solver boundary is the folded interaction kernel, not coordinate mutation
